_meta.description: Named constants used by Deep Safety screening models.

provenance.notes: Dimensionless mathematical constants such as pi.
Physical constants used across source-term, health, fire, and relief calculations.
Engineering screening defaults used where the user does not provide a case-specific value.

shared.pi.description: Pi, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
shared.pi.physical_meaning: Geometric constant used in plume normalization, circular areas, and point-source radiation geometry.

shared.gravity_standard.physical_meaning: Acceleration due to gravity used in hydrostatic and gravity-driven liquid discharge relations.

shared.universal_gas_constant.physical_meaning: Links pressure, molar volume, and absolute temperature for gases.

shared.universal_gas_constant_atm_m3.description: Universal gas constant expressed in atmosphere-cubic-meter units.
shared.universal_gas_constant_atm_m3.physical_meaning: Used in ppm-to-mg/m3 and mg/m3-to-ppm ideal-gas concentration conversions.

shared.absolute_zero_offset_c.physical_meaning: Offset required when converting Celsius temperatures into absolute temperature.

shared.reference_temperature_c.physical_meaning: Reference state for the temperature-adjusted flammability-limit screening relation.

shared.tnt_heat_of_explosion_kj_kg.description: Reference specific explosive energy of TNT used in equivalency calculations.
shared.tnt_heat_of_explosion_kj_kg.physical_meaning: Converts chemical energy release into TNT-equivalent mass for blast screening.

fire.default_radiative_fraction.description: Default radiative fraction used in fire heat-flux screening.
fire.default_radiative_fraction.physical_meaning: Fraction of total combustion energy assumed to leave the flame as radiation.

fire.default_atmospheric_transmissivity.description: Default atmospheric transmissivity for point-source fire screening.
fire.default_atmospheric_transmissivity.physical_meaning: Fraction of radiative heat assumed to reach the receptor after atmospheric attenuation.

gis.earth_radius_m.description: Mean Earth radius used in spherical-distance calculations.
gis.earth_radius_m.physical_meaning: Converts latitude/longitude differences into surface distance for GIS calculations.
